steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Ksenia!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Ksenia, are you awake? How are you feeling?

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: Feeling? I don't know. Am I supposed to feel something?

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: You're not Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: No... you were never her, why did I even ask you that...? Suka, my head—what am I even saying?

spans.text: No... you were never her, why did I even ask you that...?
my head—what am I even saying?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: I'm Mon3tr, an Operator of Rhodes Island... and also a companion to Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: Mon3tr, a familiar name, though I don't remember where I heard it... And what about you? Why are you—

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: *cough*, *cough* *cough*!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Easy now, no need to rush!

options: I am {@nickname}.
We're from Rhodes Island.
We need your help.

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: So you're indeed connected to Director Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: Rhodes Island... Serafina talked about the place. What sort of help do you need?

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: What help can I even give you, as I am now?

options: Take this back.

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: Oh, bog. Burn it.

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: I thought I'd be awake enough to destroy it myself... but it seems staying sober did not save me from this headache anyway.

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: This was written for the dead, and I hope it did not cause you any offense.

options: Sorry, but we read it.
We have questions.
You were a Sarcophagus researcher in Chernobog.
Your writing and way of addressing Kal'tsit prove this as well.

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: That was a long time ago...

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: I was just an assistant then, following Professor Ilia around and running basic data analyses. I barely had any significant ties to the project...

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: But now I see it is the very link to my ruin. I'd rather all of that had never happened at all.

options: But you still treat Kal'tsit as your director, and the research is still on your mind.
Do you know where the Sarcophagus is currently located, or where it possibly could have gone?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: It's complicated to explain, but we really have to find the Sarcophagus, we—

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: No, wait. Explain. What do you mean by 'currently located'?

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: Is it not in Chernobog?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: —What?

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: So, not only is the Sarcophagus no longer in Chernobog, the city itself has completely changed...

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: I don't know what happened, and I have no clue where it went either...

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: Sorry, I can't help you.

options: Then, do you know of...
Artyom Chaadayev?

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: You... how do you know this name?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Let's skip that first! You know him, right? Did he ever tell you anything about the Sarcophagus—

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: No... I've actually never met him.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: You what...?

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: After the incident in Chernobog that year, someone with that name contacted me by mail...

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: He called himself a friend of Professor Ilia, expressed his condolences about what happened, and showed a willingness to help out a student of his old friend and recommend me to some other laboratories within the country.

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: I once thought it a nasty joke... until the well-funded labs mentioned in the letter actually came looking for me.

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: This would happen a few more times. Indeed he gave me many rare opportunities... but even now I have no idea who this man is, or why he helped me.

options: He contacted you again recently.

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: Yes... He invited me to Deity Grypherburg, claiming there was an important project I could deploy my skills on.

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: But I was tired, what could I even do...? Looking back on what I did, all I could bring was more calamity.

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: If I had to choose where to end my miserable life, let it be the frozen soil out here in the Far North.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Doctor... what do we do now?)

options: (That project in Grypherburg sounds somewhat suspicious.)
(It sounds like she doesn't know much about it either.)
Ksenia, how did you come to know Serafina?

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: The lab had to supervise the mobile medical team in the mining district, so we got acquainted rather quickly.

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: Though we never spoke much to each other. They don't allow researchers to get too close to anyone unrelated to the project.

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: It's a bit too late now, if you wanted to find her. She left the lab with your people.

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: With that group of miners...

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: That's all I know.

options: What is the 'Oka' mentioned in your writing?
What kind of experiments did you do on the Infected miners?

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: A wretched mistake...

steps.name: Ksenia
steps.text: I didn't know... I had no idea they would use 'Oka' to do those things...

options: Calm down...
There's still time to rectify mistakes.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The Central Mining District is huge, and all eleven mines are connected by a surface transport system.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Stations are installed at every mine to deliver raw ore to be washed, processed, and stored in the warehouse.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The map seems to indicate this is the largest warehouse, and the worker dormitories are right next to it, with the south mine exit behind.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: This layout...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Storing Originium in a warehouse so close to the dormitories does not mean they trust the miners, but that they absolutely do not care about the hazard posed by active Originium particles.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Amiya.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Yes? Did you find something?

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: A chip.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: I saw it from the research lab terminal. Every miner here has a positioning chip in them. This could be why the miners we met earlier were found by the Patrol Unit.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Before the miners we were chasing chose to leave, they must have gotten rid of these.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Did they tear out the chips themselves?

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: You were right, Captain! In the south dorms, we found bandages, hemostats and other medical equipment, all Rhodes Island issue.

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: There's blood on the bandages and equipment. They turned the metal beds into a makeshift operating table, and might have performed surgery on it.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I suspect quite a big fight happened here, and the injured had to patch up their wounds.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: So those are normal findings.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Captain's asking if you've seen any tracking chips that were forcibly removed.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: No sign of any such thing.

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: No, we've swept this area.

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: As Eloysius says, the man-made damage inside and outside the warehouse seems to imply a fight broke out.

steps.name: Meticulous Operator
steps.text: But I think it was a minor scuffle, unless the fresh snow is covering up some of the aftermath...

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Alright, good work!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Captain, should we go take a look?
There is no answer, but the Phidia walks straight in the warehouse's direction.
The soldier pauses, then follows the group's footsteps.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Looks like you figured it out. To be honest, I called it a big fight, because—
The Guardswoman steps to one side and motions Elysium to help lift a waterproof sheet.
The revealed hole is filled with uneven matter covered up with a white substance that at a glance appears to be thick and dirty snow.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: This smell... doesn't seem to be snow.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Correct. It's limestone.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: And below it are corpses.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I told your Operator earlier I already investigated the area, and they took it as-is, and did not search the place any further.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I wasn't going to tell you about this...

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: They probably wanted to burn the bodies first, before realizing they couldn't get a big enough fire going and resorted to whatever was around. Quicklime to cover the stench, and the waterproof sheet to hide the hole.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: It worked, since we didn't smell the blood, yes?

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Captain's saying the dead are Patrol Unit members.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I can't say for sure. I'll climb down the hole and find out just who our unlucky customers are.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I... I'll help.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: It's fine. Just pull me up later.
Eloysius jumps right down, and stands on the edge of the hole as she wipes some limestone off.
She grabs a sleeve, quickly drops it, and goes over to check the clothes on the next body.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Alright. Could you help me back up?
Before anyone extends their hand, Mantra moves her thick tail down and wraps it around Eloysius to hoist her up, then releases her gently onto the ground.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: I've never been treated like this!

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Alright not the best time for that so sorry Captain.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I'll get to the point. Most of the bodies down there are indeed Patrol Unit members—the first and second layers, at least.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: I found this too.
The crowd looks at the fragile crystal fragment in her hand. Most of it has been charred, but the neat circuit proves it used to be a chip.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Quite a few on the ground down there. Fragments like this one, or even less.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It seems like they made a difficult choice.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: You're putting it lightly.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Captain says, the miners probably attracted the Patrol Unit with their chips, and then offed them all in one shot.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: After all, they only got the time to remove everyone else's chips after eliminating their pursuers.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: This sort of organization and ability... certainly not your garden variety miners.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Their leader definitely has military expertise... or perhaps something else.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Something else...?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: An Ursine folktale. 'The great Yurodstvo descends upon those in distress, and leads them out of dire straits'... just a tale born of boredom, though, so don't pay it much mind.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: But we ought to find them before their actions become more radical.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: After all, it's just the Patrol Unit today, but tomorrow it could be the military police, and then... it might just be the Royal Guard.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We have to find them before things get even worse.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Mantra... what are you looking for?
Mantra's eyes sweep through her surroundings, and after a long silence, Amiya hears her voice in her mind.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: That young Imperial Guardswoman reminded me of something.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: The Yurodstvo.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I think... I remember seeing this word in Dr. Kal'tsit's documents. It was related to Ursine research on demons...

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: A long, long, time ago, I too was on Ursine soil.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: After a few mishaps, I was taken to be a Yurodstvo.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Only then did I learn of an unrecorded Ursus secret, so hidden that even libraries in Sargon's City of Gold did not know it.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: The people of Ursus venerate the Yurodstvo; they believe the Yurodstvo's love transcends both the mortal realm and suffering, and this is how it has the power to lead one astray.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: So you think what's happening here is related to the Yurodstvo? But shouldn't the Yurodstvo be at the heart of Deity Grypherburg...?

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Only a hunch of mine. Everything that has happened here gives me a sense of unsettling familiarity.
Amiya follows Mantra's gaze and scans the area, but does not catch anything unusual.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Perhaps I was overthinking. But I also found some unexpected delight.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Raidian has left a beacon nearby.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: News from her? Wonderful!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: So this is how you and Raidian communicate—

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Back at Babel, Raidian was my first assistant.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: But her talent far exceeded that role, and she led her own squad after becoming an Elite Operator.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I heard there used to be many on Rhodes Island who feared you before Raidian joined us...

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Occasionally, it proves to be true.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Some of our colleagues are better at speaking than thinking, and interactions can be problematic, while I am no expert at 'explanation.'

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: That is how my 'fearsome reputation' got passed around the Rhodes Island water coolers.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: A few emergency operations where I probed into minds without prior notice, and after several rounds of exaggerated retellings, I became a witch who could stick my hand into their heads to toy with their minds.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Oh! I heard this one, in a story Theresa told me... I thought it was a Sarkaz legend.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Perhaps that was a true Sarkaz tale. The Speaker would have been defending me in saying that.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: After Raidian joined Babel, she stood among those defending my reputation.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: But today... Elysium is the flagbearer in that regard, as are you.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It's our responsibility!

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Just as I thought.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Found them.
Mantra reaches out to wipe snow off the beacon's base, and slowly the symbols on it are revealed.
She feels the faint signals left on them, and some words gradually float into her mind.

steps.name: Injured Miner
steps.text: You know what, doctor?

steps.name: Injured Miner
steps.text: We beat those Patrol Unit monsters!

steps.name: Rhodes Island Medic Operator
steps.text: Please, calm down and don't move! It's a deep wound!

steps.name: Injured Miner
steps.text: Haha! No big deal, my life would've been well-lived, even if all I managed was ending the lives of those brutes.

steps.name: Injured Miner
steps.text: How can I even relax like this?

steps.name: Injured Miner
steps.text: I never imagined this. Those high and mighty Patrol Unit guys couldn't either, I bet. That one day they would have to bow down to the Infected!

steps.name: Injured Miner
steps.text: He even asked us to spare his life? Lucky I went straight for his head!

steps.name: Injured Miner
steps.text: Rankin was right. No one can tread on us forever! We'll drag those old bastards down from their ivory towers one by one, and let them have a taste of the ground!

steps.name: Rhodes Island Medic Operator
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Rhodes Island Medic Operator
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Rankin, we've already searched the place.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: A total of ten Ursine medium-sized military trucks, with little fuel left. If everyone gets on, it'll only last us around two hundred kilometers.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Besides weapons and medicine, we found some food and water. It's not much, though it's no medicine either...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: That's pretty good already.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: I don't think these were worth the price we paid...

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Right, we discovered a container door with extra encryption on it... we need an identification code.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Hmph... Can anyone here tell me what other secrets are lying around here?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Patrolling the mines at this hour, on this day? No telling me you stumbled here from boredom.

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: I don't know...

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: I'm just a driver! No better than a burdenbeast, I go wherever the captain tells me to!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: The code or your life. Choose.

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: I don't know! I really don't know!

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: They've never given us the code to prevent the goods from running off! Only the recipient can open it!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: 'Running off'? What kind of 'thing' would do that?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Answer me! What the hell's inside those containers?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Nikto, give me one of those explosives.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Rankin, what are you—

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Just do as I say!
Rankin sticks a small Originium bomb on the container's lock. A simple move, but he almost drops it from how fast he's breathing.

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: Ah...
The door slowly falls.
Rankin sees no fewer than thirty to forty bodies packed in a ten-meter-squared container, all long deceased, with no exception.
Some had struggled to the very last, their Originium crystals piercing into neighbors with messy, bloody wounds—no doubt, they were stuffed in here still alive.
Rankin can no longer tell what stole their lives away, and he does not wish to think about it...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Did you know?

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: I, what—

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Drop the act!!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Who was it... who gave you the order?!

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: The mine boss—No, the Grand Duchess! She made us do it!

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: She cares about the miners here! Those in charge here get punished if the head count drops!

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: They always have to patch up the gap by buying some Infected with their own funds whenever one miner escapes—sometimes they get non-Infected to solve their problem, and it costs more.

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: But I have nothing to do with all that! Look, you already killed the actual bad guys!

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: I'm just a driver who listens to his boss... I'm the same as you, right...?

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: Infected, sir, please, let me go. I promise I'll desert the Patrol Unit, just pretend I died—

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: No, we're different, you and I.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: None of us willingly became Infected... but you had a choice. You could have chosen not to stand on the same side as those murderers.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: There's no reason I should forgive you.

steps.name: Hawley
steps.text: Rankin, we're done organizing the food we found.

steps.name: Hawley
steps.text: These Patrol Unit guys have it good. Tonight we can—

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: ...Father?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: Father? Is that really you?

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: Wonderful! Please, explain it to him! Tell him I'm not evil—My father's an Infected, how could I hate them?

steps.name: Hawley
steps.text: Ganea... didn't you... go to Grypherburg...?

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: I did! I really did, I didn't lie to you!

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: But I needed money to stay alive, even in Grypherburg! They don't just hand out bread and mead—being a driver was the only option I had.

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: Father, please... save me... I'll never do this again...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Hawley...
He silently stares at the oblivious elderly miner, then gestures at Hawley with his head to look at the container.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I won't try to reform him, much less release him.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: If he truly is your son...
Rankin throws a knife on the ground and walks away.

steps.name: Hawley
steps.text: No... wait...

steps.name: Hawley
steps.text: This, is not my boy, is it?

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: Father...?
Even the late autumn weather fails to prevent the corpses' rotting stench from spreading out into the air.
The old miner's gaze shifts between the mess of mangled limbs in the dark depths of the container and the tall young man before him...
Finally, he shakes his head incessantly, as if refusing to believe the truth.

steps.name: Hawley
steps.text: My son wouldn't... wouldn't say such words. He wouldn't do something this disgraceful.

steps.name: Hawley
steps.text: You're just... a damned bastard...

steps.name: Hawley
steps.text: Why—Why do you wear my son's skin? Why do you live inside his body?!
Originally trembling, the old miner explodes into a rage, knocking the man down to the ground.
His fists rain like a storm, as if trying to drive something out of the body.
The man has no strength to resist.

steps.name: Hawley
steps.text: Who are you? Who the hell are you?!

steps.name: Hawley
steps.text: Oh, poor Ganea, his soul could have been saved! This isn't how it should have been! It was you, abomination, that left him with nowhere to go!

steps.name: Hawley
steps.text: Just—

steps.name: Hawley
steps.text: Die!!!
